mistakes.note: A Choice asks what Chiara means to do with the estate, as if Anselm's wife were alive and running it, though Mara knows from the start he is widowed; it was picked and Bette had to tell her Chiara is dead.

Anselm speaks of his grandmother as dead (her old saying, she'd have liked you asking, the vines she kept, the blessing she did) while Ilse, his grandmother, is alive asleep in the house; M96 then has her alive again.
Anselm says he will tell the whole of it after the feast, not tonight, then gives the buyer, the plan and the deed one question later.
Anselm says the founders' box holds his father's debts, right after saying the debts were his wife's.

Anselm, about forty, remembers as a small boy the post-war chapel work and a priest who died before he was ten, work Ferruccio places when he himself was twelve; Bette had said the roof was done this spring.
Ferruccio, in his seventies, says Nardo's daughter was about his age, yet the reader knows her as Bette, in her late thirties; the Journal records Bette as a child when the patch was laid.
Ferruccio says Bette has a sale she doesn't want, though no one told him how she feels about it.
The move and M90 have the deed in Mara's hand; Anselm is suddenly holding it with no handover.
Bastiano Sorelli, the painter of 1720, is added as a Known NPC with looks and a portrait in present-day dress.
Anselm's knowledge gets near-duplicate entries for the same refusal, and several NPC entries are written in the first person.
Plot Thread now says Anselm left the wine at her door and went to the cellar with the sale papers while he was in the yard drinking it with Mara.
The World Change has Anselm put Haldane in the east room while he was at the chapel all morning, adds to Mara's Known facts an arrival she never learned, and never reaches the page.
The Loose End for Ferruccio's half-past-seven visit closes a dozen rounds after he came.
Mara takes the deed to lock away but it is never put back in her carrying, while Ferruccio's float, chisel and pencil stay there after he packed his tools.
The World Bible never grew: Ferruccio, Nardo Sorell, Don Sisto, the found deed and the fire on Sestini's ridge were never added.
Portrait of Anselm Corra redrawn clean-shaven with a buzz cut; he has a short beard on the page and in every scene picture.
Scene drawn near-photographic, not watercolour (again at M19 and M58), with an electric lamp lit in a chapel the page lights by lantern alone and no scaffold.
The house shows several lit windows and a porch light where the page has it dark but for one window.

choices.reason: Mostly three distinct, fitting paths and picks steer the hunt, but one round offered only two and the round-10 Choice treated dead Chiara as alive and was picked.

surprise.reason: The deed in the threshold and Nardo Sorell's envelope land fairly, but they come from the PC digging; Bette's sabotage, Ilse's heart and Haldane never surface on the page.

threads.reason: Anselm's wine visit fires and bends to Mara's absence, but Bette's follow-up sits at 'not yet' for 25 rounds, Ilse's errand slips a day, and only ten hours pass toward the feast.

characters.reason: Anselm, Bette and Ferruccio each have a voice and reasons; Anselm's instant confession after 'not tonight' and Ferruccio knowing Bette's mind are lapses.

continuity.reason: Anselm speaks of his living grandmother as dead, and the post-war timeline muddles who was a child when, plus a deed that changes hands unseen.

pacing.reason: Every reply adds a fact or a shift, though the plaster investigation runs slow over many fine-grained beats.

prose.reason: Concrete, tactile and varied in one voice; tics of glasses set down and turned a quarter turn, and a few muddled lines.

pictures.reason: Scenes show the right people and moments, but several slip into photographic style with electric lights, and Anselm's redrawn portrait lost his beard.

secrets.reason: The deed is found by knocking, probing and digging; Anselm's sale comes from his own mouth after a won Check; Bette's sabotage and Ilse's heart stay hidden.

agency.reason: The Narrator carries out each move as given and keeps Mara's words to what she said.

stakes.reason: Checks are frequent and failures cost Anselm's warmth for a few beats, but the ruined lettering is undone a reply later and trivial asks get rolled.

state.reason: A stale picked Choice, a Plot Thread placing Anselm in the cellar while on the page, a World Change never shown, lore that never grew and loose items.

romance.reason: Anselm's dawn visit with the first wine has real ache and he lets slip more than he means, but from there the story becomes a hunt for the deed; Mara's desire is never felt from inside and touch is limited to a hand closing hers over keys.
